comments.body:
Root cause and deterministic reproduction (py3.12 GIL build, mechanism-level; no py3.14t interpreter on this host).

Observation: run 41749721339 `sweep (py3.14t)` fails only this test with "the bound op-cert key ... does not exist". Holding the test's worker thread 200 ms between `Thread.start()` and its first line reproduces the identical error on py3.12 every run; the unmodified test passes there.

Mechanism: `run_mcp` waits for the in-flight gauge to reach 0 before `mcp_server.main()` deletes the signer's key copy. A drained tool call was only counted once its worker ran `gauge.track` — the first line of the instrumented wrapper. FastMCP hands calls to an AnyIO worker (`_thread_offloaded`), so between the worker picking the call up and that line the gauge read 0. If the transport stopped in that window, `run_mcp` returned, the key copy was deleted, and the close then committed STATUS and failed to sign. The test's fake server had the same gap (bare `threading.Thread`). Free-threaded CPython runs the serving thread in parallel with the worker, which makes the window reachable; the GIL build usually lets the new thread run first. The second ticket hypothesis (another test cleaning `rebar-opcert-*`) is not needed to explain the failure: the key path in the log belongs to this test's own `box_binding`, which this test itself cleans up.

Fix (in `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py`): a drained tool is counted on the event loop when it is handed to a worker (`InFlightGauge.admit`, same refusal while draining), and the worker runs the uncounted body. A start/abandon handshake makes exactly one side release the count: the worker when the body ends, or the abandoning caller if the worker had not started — then the body is skipped, as AnyIO already skips a cancelled call. The count stays 1 per call.

Tests (fail before, pass after): `test_mcp_tool_offload.py::test_a_drained_call_is_counted_before_its_worker_runs_it`, `test_mcp_drain_signing_iguanodon.py::test_close_picked_up_but_not_started_when_the_server_stops_never_runs`. The existing end-to-end test now runs through the real `wire_health` + AnyIO offload instead of a bare thread.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The scheduled **Test Suite (mirror)** leg `sweep (py3.14t)` (free-threaded CPython 3.14, `-n 4 --dist worksteal`) failed `tests/unit/test_mcp_drain_signing_iguanodon.py::test_close_reaching_signing_after_the_server_stops_ends_certified` in runs 41696793491 and 41749721339 (the only failure in the latter; py3.14, py3.15 and macOS passed it). A close in flight when the server stopped ended `{'signed': False, 'cause': 'sign_failed'}`: "the bound op-cert key '/tmp/rebar-opcert-<random>/opcert-key' does not exist (the composed signer's key copy is absent)".

## Root cause

`run_mcp` waits for the in-flight gauge to reach 0 before `mcp_server.main()` deletes the signer's key copy. A drained tool call (`DRAINED_TOOLS`) was counted only when its worker ran `gauge.track`, the first line of the instrumented wrapper. FastMCP hands each call to an AnyIO worker (`_thread_offloaded`), so between the worker picking the call up and that line the gauge read 0. A transport that stopped in that window let `run_mcp` return, the key copy was deleted, and the close then committed STATUS and failed to sign. The test's fake server had the same gap (a bare `threading.Thread`). Free-threaded CPython runs the serving thread in parallel with the worker, which makes the window reachable.

Reproduction (py3.12, mechanism-level; no py3.14t interpreter on the host): holding the test's worker 200 ms between start and its first line produces the CI error on every run. The key path in the log belongs to the test's own `box_binding`, so a second hypothesis (another test deleting `rebar-opcert-*` dirs) is not needed to explain it.

## Fix

In `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py`, a drained tool is counted on the event loop when it is handed to a worker (`InFlightGauge.admit`, with the same refusal while draining), and the worker runs the uncounted body. `_CountedHandoff` releases the count exactly once: the worker when the body ends, or the abandoning caller if the worker had not started, in which case the body is skipped, as AnyIO already skips a cancelled call. Each call still counts 1.

Landed as Gerrit change 3284, merged `561dc66af8e`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [non-codebase] A deterministic local reproduction is recorded on this ticket.
  provenance: environment=local-dev-macos-py3.12; principal=Rebar Bot Nava; privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=simulation — the worker-start delay was injected into a scratch copy of the test and run locally; the result and mechanism are recorded in this ticket's comments.
- [x] A regression test fails before the fix and passes after it: `tests/unit/test_mcp_tool_offload.py::test_a_drained_call_is_counted_before_its_worker_runs_it` and `tests/unit/test_mcp_drain_signing_iguanodon.py::test_close_picked_up_but_not_started_when_the_server_stops_never_runs` fail on the parent of `561dc66af8e` and pass on it.
